content: Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under the age of six. It is crucial to keep this medication out of the reach of children. If an accidental overdose occurs, contact your doctor or a poison control center immediately. Ferrous sulfate provides the iron necessary for the body to produce red blood cells. It is used to treat or prevent iron-deficiency anemia, a condition characterized by a low number of red blood cells due to factors such as pregnancy, poor diet, excessive bleeding, or other medical conditions. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Ferrous sulfate is available in various forms, including regular, coated, and extended-release tablets; regular and extended-release capsules; and oral liquids such as syrups, drops, and elixirs. It is typically taken three times a day between meals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take ferrous sulfate exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. While symptoms of iron deficiency may improve within a few days, severe iron deficiency may require treatment with ferrous sulfate for up to six months. This medication should be taken on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after eating. Ferrous sulfate drops come with a special dropper for measuring the dose; ask your pharmacist to demonstrate its use. The drops can be placed directly in the mouth or mixed with water or fruit juice (but not milk). Do not crush or chew regular, coated, or extended-release tablets, and do not open regular or extended-release capsules; swallow them whole. Before taking ferrous sulfate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ferrous sulfate, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and drugs), or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially chloramphenicol, cimetidine (Tagamet), levodopa (Larodopa, Sinemet), methyldopa (Aldomet), penicillamine, and vitamins. If you are also taking cinoxacin (Cinobac), ciprofloxacin (Cipro), demeclocycline, doxycycline, enoxacin (Penetrex), levofloxacin (Levaquin), lomefloxacin (Maxaquin), methacycline, minocycline, nalidixic acid (NegGram), norfloxacin (Noroxin), ofloxacin (Floxin), oxytetracycline, sparfloxacin (Zagam), or tetracycline, take these medications three hours after or two hours before taking ferrous sulfate. Avoid taking antacids at the same time as ferrous sulfate; space them as far apart as possible. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had ulcers, colitis, or intestinal disease. Additionally, notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ferrous sulfate, contact your doctor. Incorporate dietary sources of iron, such as fish, meat (especially liver), and fortified cereals and breads, into a well-balanced diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ferrous sulfate may cause side effects. Your stools may turn dark, which is a harmless effect. Liquid forms of the medication may stain your teeth; mix each dose with water or fruit juice and clean your teeth weekly by rubbing them with a small amount of baking soda. Contact your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as constipation or stomach upset. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of the reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to ferrous sulfate. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
